# package mbcsv

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-modbus-capture/mbcsv"
```

Package mbcsv reads and writes captures as CSV. Long CSV (.mbcap.csv, docs/FORMAT.md section 4) is lossless: one row per record, the same records as JSON Lines, PDUs as lowercase hex. Wide CSV (section 5) is a one-way view of raw register and bit values over time, sample and hold applied.

## Constants

```go
const MaxRecordLen = 4 << 20
```

MaxRecordLen is the largest CSV record (row) a Reader accepts.

Columns are the long CSV columns, in the order a Writer writes them.

### type WideStats

```go
type WideStats struct {
	// Rows is the number of rows written, column names not counted.
	Rows int
	// Columns is the number of value columns.
	Columns int
	// Skipped counts FC01–04 samples left out: exception responses and
	// responses whose size does not match the request.
	Skipped int
}
```

WideStats says what WriteWide left out.

#### func WriteWide

```go
func WriteWide(w io.Writer, c *capture.Capture) (WideStats, error)
```

WriteWide writes the wide CSV view of c: one row per sample time of an FC01–04 sample, one column per (target, function, address), named "\<target>/\<fc>/\<address>" with the function code as two hex digits. Each cell holds the latest value sampled at or before the row's time (sample and hold), or is empty before the first sample of its address. Values are raw: 0 or 1 for coils and discrete inputs, unsigned 16-bit words for registers. Samples are taken in time order; samples at the same time share a row.

The view cannot be read back: it drops request PDUs, other functions and per-sample identity.
